data.title: The Séance
data.rumour: Madame Orsolya's doing a séance for the Harrow widow.
about: Marv Kettle sells you a writing box initialled E.H. from the study of the late Edmund Harrow (§{marvBox}). Madame Orsolya asks to borrow it for a séance for his widow, Ida, because Edmund left no will anyone can find and his nephew Clement inherits everything without one (§{orsolyaBorrows}).

At the séance (§{seance}) Edmund speaks through Orsolya: he put the will where he always put things. You realise the box has a false bottom. Open it at the table, revealing a will leaving everything to Ida and his fountain pen to Clement (The Will), or keep the lid shut and find the will and a lining of old banknotes at home, which makes the box worth far more (Shut the Lid).

harrowBox.name: Writing box, initialled E.H.
tells: Walnut, brass corners, a sloped writing lid. 1920s.
The inside is a quarter of an inch shallower than the outside. A false bottom.

marvBox.title: Marv Kettle brings in a dead man's writing box

text: Marv Kettle, house clearances. Cleared out old Edmund Harrow's study up on Fern Hill. The nephew wanted the lot gone by Friday.
Nice writing box. E.H. on the lid. The nephew said "sell it, it's just a box".

orsolyaBorrows.title: Madame Orsolya wants to borrow the box for a séance

text: Madame Orsolya, from the boardwalk. Palms, cards, and the occasional dead husband.
I am holding a séance for the Harrow widow. Edmund Harrow, God rest him, died without leaving a will that anyone can find. The nephew gets everything unless one turns up.

then.text: I need something of Edmund's to call him by. I hear his writing box came through here, but I see it has gone again. A pity.

steps.text: That writing box. E.H. That was his. May I borrow it, for one evening? And you must come. The dead are calmer when the owner of the object is in the room.

then.text: {placed:seance}, after dark. The parlor at the end of the boardwalk, with the fairy lights. Do not wear anything that jingles.

then.toast: Calendar: the séance at Madame Orsolya's, {placed:seance} night

choose.label: "It's stock. It stays on the shelf."

then.text: Then Edmund will have to find his own way. They usually do, eventually.

steps.narrate: Madame Orsolya's parlor, after dark. The fairy lights are turned down. Edmund Harrow's writing box sits beside the crystal ball, and everybody's hands are on the table.

steps.text: Can we get on? I have the solicitor at nine.
Edmund Harrow. Edmund. We have your box. Come and sit with us.

steps.narrate: The candle flames lie down flat. The crystal ball goes white. And then Orsolya speaks in a voice that is not Orsolya's.

steps.text: IDA. Ida, I wrote it. I put it where I always put things. Why does nobody look where I put things?
Edmund? Where? Where did you put it?
This is a parlor trick. Madame, I'm not paying for a parlor trick.

narrate.then: You know where. You put the loupe on that box the day it came in: a quarter of an inch too shallow inside. A false bottom.
narrate.else: Your thumb finds it without you meaning to: the floor of the box sits a quarter of an inch too high. A false bottom.

choose.label: Open the false bottom, here at the table

then.narrate: Under the false bottom: a will, handwritten, witnessed, dated last spring. Everything to Ida. To Clement, "my fountain pen, which he has always admired, and my advice, which he has always ignored".

text: Contest away, dear. You have the pen to do it with.
Thank you. Please, take this for your trouble. And the box is yours. I couldn't look at it.

choose.label: Say nothing. Keep the lid shut.

then.narrate: The candles stand back up. The ball clears. Orsolya opens her eyes and looks straight at you, and you look at the curtains.

then.text: Well, that settles it. Nothing. Good evening, Aunt Ida.

then.narrate: At home you open the false bottom. The will, and under it, a lining of old banknotes, folded flat: Edmund's rainy-day money. The box is worth a great deal more than you paid.

tells: Walnut, brass corners. The false bottom is lined with old banknotes. And a will nobody will ever read.

epilogue.line: Ida Harrow kept the house on Fern Hill. Clement Harrow kept the pen.
Clement Harrow sold his uncle's house within the month. Madame Orsolya has not read your palm since.
